text: @sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的插件，为 pi-ai 的 OpenAI Codex 路由提供 ChatGPT 设备码登录。它向 LLM 服务注册 openai-codex 的认证控制器，并将 OAuth 凭据保存在 DSH 的本地凭据文件中。用户可以发起设备授权、查看登录状态、取消登录或退出登录；凭据存储支持并发写入协调。适合希望在 DSH 中使用 ChatGPT 账号认证 Codex 模型的用户。登录需要访问 auth.openai.com，凭据默认存于 $DSH_HOME/.llm-oauth.json。

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth adds ChatGPT device-code login for DSH's Codex route, with local OAuth storage and login, status, cancel, and logout controls. It connects to auth.openai.com; credentials default to $DSH_HOME/.llm-oauth.json.
想用 ChatGPT 账号登录 DSH 里的 Codex 模型。
能不能用设备验证码给 DSH 的 OpenAI Codex 路由授权？
I want to sign in to the Codex model route in DSH with a ChatGPT device code.
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth 的功能「ChatGPT 设备码登录」：在 DSH 中启动 OpenAI Codex OAuth 设备授权，显示验证码和验证地址，并提供取消或登出操作。
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth 的功能「本地 OAuth 凭据存储」：认证凭据写入 DSH 凭据 JSON 文件，支持读取、更新和删除，并协调并发写入。
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth 须知：OAuth 凭据写入 $DSH_HOME/.llm-oauth.json；Windows 需保护目录。（src/auth-store.ts:315-317）
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth 使用前须知：设备授权流程连接 auth.openai.com。（见 src/openai-codex-auth.ts:25-26）

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · @sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

An independently versioned, installable OpenAI Codex device-login plugin for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`. It contributes OAuth storage and the `openai-codex` interactive-auth controller without adding a second model adapter.

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth
```

The bundle inserts one `openai-codex-auth` configuration row. Remove the same package to unload its controller and credential contribution without changing the base adapter:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove @sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth
```

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Install：The Models page then offers a ChatGPT device-code login. OAuth requests run in the DSH Node process; on Node 24, proxy environment variables require `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` (or `--use-env-proxy`).

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Configuration：Structured credentials are stored at `$DSH_HOME/.llm-oauth.json`. `path` overrides that file, `dshHome` changes the default home, `lockTimeoutMs` defaults to 30 seconds, `lockStaleMs` to 60 seconds, `loginTimeoutMs` to 16 minutes, and `startupTimeoutMs` to 30 seconds.

```yaml
- id: openai-codex-auth
  name: '@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth'
  config:
    dshHome: ~/.dsh

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Configuration：The store serializes mutations in process and across processes. A provider generation prevents a login completing after logout from restoring a deleted credential. POSIX files are atomically replaced at mode `0600`; Windows users must protect `DSH_HOME` with their account ACL. Browser RPC state never includes tokens or raw provider responses.

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Extension Role：The plugin claims `openai-codex` in `ctx.piAiCredentials` and registers its controller on `ctx.llm`. `dsh-llm-pi-ai` snapshots that mapping with each `Models` collection, so an active request retains its original store while later requests observe load or unload. A second plugin claiming the provider fails loud.

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Development：The current DSH release has no published pi-ai credential contribution seam. Develop this package beside the SIPI-patched `deepseek-harness` checkout that provides `ctx.piAiCredentials` and `ctx.llm.registerProviderAuth()`. Installing against an unpatched upstream release fails at startup rather than silently losing OAuth persistence. See [compatibility notes](COMPATIBILITY.zh.md).
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · What the model sees：Nothing. `openai-codex` login state and OAuth credentials stay outside model requests.
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Token effect：Zero direct token effect.
@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · KV Cache effect：Independent of cache identity. The selected `openai-codex` model request determines provider cache behavior.

@sipi/dsh-openai-codex-auth README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **One login method** — only OpenAI's device authorization is exposed.
- **pi-ai catalog dependency** — activation fails when the installed catalog does not expose `openai-codex` OAuth.
